q.s: Which Harappan site in India was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021, the first Indus site in India on the list?
q.x: Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat) was inscribed in 2021; Mohenjodaro, listed in 1980, is in Pakistan.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in present-day India?
q.x: Mohenjodaro is in Sindh, Pakistan; Dholavira, Lothal and Rakhigarhi are in India.

q.s: The Harappan script was mostly written in which direction?
q.x: The pictographic Harappan script was mostly written from right to left.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Harappan script is correct?
o: It has not yet been deciphered.
It was deciphered by James Prinsep.
It is an early form of the Brahmi alphabet.
q.x: The script, with about 400+ signs, remains undeciphered; Prinsep deciphered Brahmi, not the Harappan script.

q.s: Who identified the horned figure on the Pashupati seal of Mohenjodaro as 'proto-Shiva'?
q.x: John Marshall called the figure proto-Shiva (Pashupati, 'lord of animals'); the reading is an inference, since the script is undeciphered.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT generally associated with Harappan religion?
q.x: No temple has been identified at Harappan sites; Mother Goddess, Pashupati and pipal worship are attested.

q.s: Which classical writer complained in his 'Natural History' about the drain of Roman gold to India?
q.x: Pliny's Natural History, in Latin, puts the drain at about 50 million sesterces a year.

q.s: The port 'Masulia' (Maisolia) mentioned by Ptolemy as a textile market is identified with:
q.x: Ptolemy's Masulia/Maisolia is identified with Machilipatnam.

q.s: In the Early Vedic period, the term 'Vaishya' is derived from which social unit?
q.x: Vaishya derives from Vis; the units in ascending order were Kula, Grama, Vis and Jana.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Early Vedic society is correct?
o: Jana was the smallest social unit.
q.x: Monogamy was usual; the family was patriarchal, patrilineal and patrilocal, and Kula (family) was the smallest unit.

q.s: Where did Gautama Buddha attain Mahaparinirvana?
q.x: The Buddha died at Kushinagar at the age of 80; Sarnath is where he gave his first sermon.

q.s: Which of the following places is NOT among the four great places of pilgrimage linked with the Buddha's birth, enlightenment, first sermon and death?
q.x: The four are Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar; Vaishali hosted the Second Council.

q.s: The Fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalavana in Kashmir was presided over by:
q.x: Vasumitra presided, with Ashvaghosha as deputy; Moggaliputta Tissa presided over the Third Council.

q.s: Which of the following Buddhist councils is NOT correctly paired with its venue?
q.x: The Third Council, under Moggaliputta Tissa, was held at Pataliputra.

q.s: Nagarjunakonda, known as 'Dakshina Gaya', was the capital of which dynasty?
q.x: Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri) was the Ikshvaku capital; it now lies under the Nagarjuna Sagar.

q.s: Which Buddhist sect had its centre at Nagarjunakonda?
q.x: Nagarjunakonda was the Aparasaila centre; the Purvasaila sect was centred at Amaravati.

q.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved under which Rashtrakuta king?
q.x: The rock-cut Kailasa temple is a work of the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

q.s: The Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves of Kharavela in Odisha belong to which religion?
q.x: The Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves were cut for Jain monks under Kharavela.

q.s: Which Mauryan ruler, a grandson of Ashoka, is called the 'Ashoka of Jainism'?
q.x: Samprati spread Jainism as Ashoka spread Buddhism.

q.s: Which of the following rulers was NOT a patron of Jainism?
q.x: Pushyamitra Sunga was a Brahmanical ruler; Samprati, Kumarapala and Amoghavarsha I patronised Jainism.

q.s: In Kautilya's Arthashastra, the term 'Vishti' refers to:
q.x: Vishti was unpaid forced labour (Telugu 'vetti'); karmakara was wage labour and stridhana a woman's own property.

q.s: Which of the following Arthashastra terms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
q.x: Moksha meant divorce; karmakara was wage labour.

q.s: According to the Allahabad Pillar inscription, the king of Devarashtra defeated by Samudragupta was:
q.x: Kubera ruled Devarashtra; Ugrasena ruled Palakka, Damana Erandapalle and Mantaraja Kurala.

q.s: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) describing Samudragupta's conquests was composed by:
q.x: Harisena, Samudragupta's court poet, composed it; Ravikirti composed the Aihole inscription.

q.s: In Gupta administration, the district-level unit was known as the:
q.x: The vishaya (district) was larger than the vithi, a group of villages; the bhukti was a province.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an administrative unit of the Gupta period?
q.x: Valanadu was a Chola unit; Gupta units were bhukti, vishaya, vithi and grama.

q.s: Which Gupta ruler is depicted playing the veena on his coins?
q.x: The lyrist type belongs to Samudragupta; the lion-slayer type is of Chandragupta II.

q.s: The 'King-Queen' type gold coins showing the king with Kumaradevi were issued by:
q.x: Chandragupta I's coins show him with his Lichchhavi queen Kumaradevi.

q.s: The Chinese pilgrim who visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana was:
q.x: Hiuen Tsang stayed in India in Harsha's time; Fa-Hien came under Chandragupta II.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Harshavardhana is NOT correct?
o: He was a patron of Mahayana Buddhism.
q.x: Though a Mahayana patron, Harsha continued to patronise Brahmanical scholars.

q.s: In Chola administration, the official who wrote down the king's oral orders on palm leaf was the:
q.x: The Tirumandira-olai wrote the orders; the Olai-nayagam checked and countersigned them.

q.s: Which of the following Chola officials is NOT correctly matched with the role?
o: Adhikari - Wrote the king's oral orders
q.x: The Adhikari supervised local bodies; the Tirumandira-olai wrote the king's oral orders.

q.s: Who was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
q.x: Razia, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled 1236-40.

q.s: Razia Sultan married which governor of Bhatinda before marching on Delhi?
q.x: She married Altuniya and was killed after their march on Delhi failed.

q.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, the tax called 'Charai' was levied on:
q.x: Charai was the grazing tax and Ghari the house tax.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Alauddin Khalji?
o: Using the biswa as a unit of land measurement
q.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary; Alauddin curbed the iqtadars and village headmen.

q.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq transferred his capital from Delhi to Devagiri (Daulatabad) in:
q.x: The transfer was made in 1327.

q.s: The token currency of copper and brass coins was introduced by:
q.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued token coins on the model of Kublai Khan's paper money.

q.s: Which Sultan of Delhi made the iqtas hereditary?
q.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq made the iqtas hereditary; Alauddin had kept them under strict control.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
q.x: Token currency was introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Firoz abolished about 24 taxes and kept the four Islamic ones.

q.s: Abdur Razzaq, the envoy of Shah Rukh, visited Vijayanagara during the reign of:
q.x: Abdur Razzaq came in 1443-44 under Deva Raya II; Nicolo Conti came under Deva Raya I.

q.s: Which of the following foreign travellers did NOT visit the Vijayanagara Empire?
q.x: Nikitin visited the Bahmani kingdom; the other three described Vijayanagara.

q.s: The Battle of Khanwa (1527) was fought between Babur and:
q.x: At Khanwa Babur used trenches and barricades against Rana Sanga's war elephants.

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought by Babur?
q.x: The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought by Akbar's forces against Hemu.

q.s: Akbar conferred the title 'Jagat Guru' on the Jain monk:
q.x: Hiravijaya Suri became Jagat Guru; Jinachandra Suri received the title Yuga Pradhan.

q.s: Akbar's land grant on which the city of Amritsar grew was made to:
q.x: The grant to Guru Ram Das let Amritsar grow.

q.s: By the end of Akbar's reign, the Mughal Empire was divided into how many subas?
q.x: Akbar had 12 subas in 1580 and 15 by the end of his reign; Aurangzeb's empire had 21.

q.s: Aurangzeb spent roughly the last 25 years of his reign campaigning in the:
q.x: The Deccan wars took up about the last 25 years of his reign.

q.s: The jizya, abolished by Akbar in 1564, was reimposed in 1679 by:
q.x: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya in 1679.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Akbar?
o: Stopping enslavement of prisoners of war
q.x: Akbar abolished the pilgrim tax (1563) and jizya (1564), stopped enslaving war prisoners (1562) and built the Ibadat Khana (1575).

q.s: The white marble used in the Taj Mahal came mainly from:
q.x: The marble came from Makrana in Rajasthan.

q.s: Mumtaz Mahal, for whom the Taj Mahal was built, was originally named:
q.x: Arjumand Banu Begum; Mehr-un-Nisa was Nur Jahan.

q.s: Akbar's painting atelier, which had more than 100 painters under Abdus Samad, was called the:
q.x: The Tasvir Khana was the royal painting workshop.

q.s: Mughal painting reached its zenith under which emperor?
q.x: Mughal painting peaked under Jahangir, when the halo behind the emperor's head first appeared.

q.s: Vallabhacharya, who came from a Telugu Brahmin family and visited Krishnadevaraya's court, mainly preached Krishna bhakti in:
q.x: Vallabha preached mainly in Gujarat; Chaitanya preached in Bengal.

q.s: 'Chapakudu', the practice of inter-dining in Palnadu, is associated with:
q.x: Brahmanaidu, minister in Palnadu, promoted inter-dining (Chapakudu).

q.s: The Shattari Sufi saint Shah Muhammad Ghaus of Gwalior was the spiritual guide of:
q.x: Shah Muhammad Ghaus guided Humayun and Tansen and wrote the Jawahir-e-Khamsa.

q.s: In 1498 Vasco da Gama made landfall at Kappad, near:
q.x: He landed at Kappad near Calicut, guided from Malindi by a Gujarati pilot.

q.s: Vasco da Gama's first voyage to India (1497) was commissioned by:
q.x: King Manuel I of Portugal commissioned the voyage.

q.s: Bombay came to Charles II of England in 1661 as the dowry of Catherine of Braganza, a princess of:
q.x: Catherine was Portuguese; Bombay was taken from the Portuguese.

q.s: During the Revolt of 1857, Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt at:
q.x: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt in Lucknow and proclaimed her son Birjis Qadr Nawab of Awadh.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Revolt of 1857?
q.x: Ranjit Singh died in 1839; Tantia Tope, Lakshmibai and Kunwar Singh led the revolt.

q.s: The Treaty of Yandabo (1826) ended which war?
q.x: Yandabo ended the First Anglo-Burmese War.

q.s: Which territory was NOT ceded to the British by the Treaty of Yandabo (1826)?
q.x: Yandabo gave Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim; Pegu was annexed after the Second Anglo-Burmese War (1852).

q.s: Which colonial law of 1878 declared forests to be state property and fuelled tribal discontent?
q.x: The Indian Forest Act, 1878 made forests state property, curbing tribal rights of use.

q.s: Wilkinson's Rule (1837), under which tribal areas were governed through Munda-Manki chiefs, applied to:
q.x: Wilkinson's Rule applied to the Kolhan, not the Santhal Parganas.

q.s: The cotton slump that led Deccan peasants to default and lose land to moneylenders followed the end of the:
q.x: The cotton boom of the American Civil War ended with the war, leaving ryots indebted (the Deccan Riots of 1875 followed).

q.s: The Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 replaced the Press and Registration of Books Act of:
q.x: The 2023 Act replaced the 1867 Act; the RNI is now the Press Registrar General of India.

q.s: The World Press Freedom Index is released by:
q.x: The index is published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), not UNESCO.

q.s: Which was the first all-India trade union body, founded in 1920?
q.x: AITUC (1920) came first; then INTUC (1947), Hind Mazdoor Sabha (1948) and CITU (1970).

q.s: Which of the following trade union bodies was founded in 1947, closely linked to the Congress?
q.x: INTUC was founded in 1947; CITU came in 1970.

q.s: Raja Rammohan Roy's 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' ('Gift to Monotheists') was written in:
q.x: Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin was in Persian; Precepts of Jesus (1820) was in English.

q.s: Which newspaper of Rammohan Roy was a Persian weekly started in 1822?
q.x: Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822) was in Persian; Sambad Kaumudi (1821) was a Bengali weekly.

q.s: Which organisation, led by Radhakant Deb in 1830, opposed the ban on sati?
q.x: Radhakant Deb's Dharma Sabha defended sati against Bentinck's ban of 1829.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Brahmo Samaj?
q.x: No images were allowed in Brahmo halls.

q.s: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, leader of the Young Bengal Movement, taught at:
q.x: Derozio taught at Hindu College; his students formed the Academic Association (1828).

q.s: Gurram Jashuva, the first modern Telugu Dalit poet, wrote which work in 1941?
q.x: Jashuva wrote Gabbilam; Paleru is Boyi Bhimanna's play.

q.s: Gurram Jashuva was popularly known by the title:
q.x: Jashuva was 'Kavi Kokila'; 'Kavi Samrat' was Viswanatha Satyanarayana.

q.s: Jyotiba Phule opened his first school for girls at Pune in:
q.x: Phule's girls' school was opened in 1848; he founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873.

q.s: Sree Narayana Guru consecrated the Shiva idol at Aruvippuram in:
q.x: The Aruvippuram consecration was in 1888; the SNDP Yogam came in 1903.

q.s: Dr. Ambedkar gave up separate electorates for the Depressed Classes in return for reserved seats under the:
q.x: Ambedkar signed the Poona Pact (1932) after Gandhi's fast against the Communal Award.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Ambedkar-Gandhi debate of 1932 is correct?
o: Ambedkar refused to sign the Poona Pact.
The Poona Pact extended separate electorates.
Gandhi supported separate electorates for Dalits.
Ambedkar supported the separate electorate given by the Communal Award.
q.x: Ambedkar backed separate electorates but signed the Poona Pact, accepting reserved seats instead.

q.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism in October 1956 at:
q.x: He embraced Buddhism at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur; Yeola is where he made his 1935 declaration.

q.s: In 1935 Ambedkar declared that though born a Hindu he would not die a Hindu, at:
q.x: The Yeola declaration was made on 13 October 1935.

q.s: The rising of Titu Mir in Bengal in 1831 is associated with:
q.x: Titu Mir built a bamboo fort at Narkelberia in 1831.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Titu Mir - Revolutionary phase of the Faraizi movement from 1840
q.x: The revolutionary Faraizi phase from 1840 was led by Dudu Miyan; Titu Mir is linked with Narkelberia (1831).

q.s: Surendranath Banerjee's Indian National Conference merged with the Indian National Congress in:
q.x: The Conference merged with the INC in 1886.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Surendranath Banerjee is correct?
o: He started the Amrita Bazar Patrika.
He presided over the Surat session of 1907.
q.x: He started The Bengalee; Rash Behari Ghosh presided at Surat, and he passed the ICS in 1869.

q.s: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, though radical in politics, opposed which social measure of 1891?
q.x: Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill (1891), showing his social conservatism.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT one of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio?
q.x: Gokhale was a Moderate leader.

q.s: The Communal Award of August 1932 was announced by:
q.x: British PM Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award on 16 August 1932.

q.s: Which Congress session of March 1931 endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
q.x: The Karachi session endorsed the Pact and adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution.

q.s: Who first took over leadership of the Salt Satyagraha after Gandhi's arrest in May 1930?
q.x: Abbas Tyabji led first; after his arrest Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana raid.

q.s: Who likened Gandhi's Dandi March to Napoleon's march from Elba to Paris?
q.x: Subhas Chandra Bose made the comparison.

q.s: Why did the youth and the left oppose the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931?
o: It made Gandhi attend the First Round Table Conference
It did not save Bhagat Singh and his comrades
It ended the Salt laws completely
q.x: Irwin refused to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.

q.s: In the Congress presidential election of 1939, Subhas Chandra Bose defeated:
q.x: Bose defeated Gandhi's nominee Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri but resigned in April 1939.

q.s: After resigning the Congress presidency in 1939, Subhas Chandra Bose formed the:
q.x: Bose formed the Forward Bloc in 1939.

q.s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu, killed in police firing at Minchalapadu in 1922, led the satyagraha against the 'pullari' tax in:
q.x: Pullari was a tax on grazing cattle in forest lands; the Palnadu movement began in 1921.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Palnadu satyagraha is correct?
o: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed at Minchalapadu in 1922.
Pullari was a tax on cutting timber.
q.x: Pullari taxed cattle grazing; the movement began in 1921 and officials were boycotted at Macherla.

q.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, leader of the Chirala-Perala movement, was known by the title:
q.x: Gopalakrishnayya was 'Andhra Ratna'; T. Prakasam was 'Andhra Kesari'.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of person and title is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Ketana was 'Abhinava Dandi'; Andhra Ratna was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya.

q.s: Bhimavaram, where police fired on a crowd on 17 August 1942 during the Quit India Movement, is in:
q.x: Bhimavaram is in West Godavari.

q.s: Vallabhbhai Patel presided over which Congress session that adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution?
q.x: Patel presided at Karachi (March 1931); Nehru drafted the resolution.

q.s: In the Interim Government formed on 2 September 1946, Vallabhbhai Patel held:
q.x: Patel held Home with I&B; Nehru held External Affairs and Liaquat Ali Khan Finance.

q.s: Article 371D, implementing the Six-Point Formula for Andhra Pradesh, was inserted by the:
q.x: The 32nd Amendment (1973) inserted Article 371D.

q.s: NTR's 1986 decision to raise the BC quota to 44%, later struck down by the High Court, was based on the report of the:
q.x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission's report was the basis.

q.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949) demanded:
o: A state of all Telugu-speaking areas
q.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha sought one state of all Telugu areas, including Telangana.

q.s: Potti Sriramulu was born in which city?
q.x: He was born in Madras; his ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore district.

q.s: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after a fast of how many days?
q.x: He fasted from 19 October 1952 and died on the 58th day.

q.s: Potti Sriramulu's fast for a separate Andhra State was held at whose house in Mylapore?
q.x: The fast was at Bulusu Sambamurthy's house in Mylapore, Madras.

q.s: The High Court of Andhra State, set up on 5 July 1954, was located at:
q.x: The High Court sat at Guntur; Kurnool was the capital. Koka Subba Rao was its first Chief Justice.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra State (1953-56) is correct?
o: Its High Court was at Kurnool.
T. Prakasam was its first Chief Minister.
K.V. Ranga Reddy was its Deputy Chief Minister.
q.x: Prakasam was the first CM; N. Sanjiva Reddy was Deputy CM, the capital was Kurnool and the High Court at Guntur.

q.s: OCTOPUS, set up in Andhra Pradesh in 2007, is a:
q.x: OCTOPUS is the anti-terror force; the Greyhounds are the anti-Naxal commandos.

q.s: The first session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal (1950) wanted which city as the capital?
q.x: The Warangal session wanted Hyderabad as the capital.

q.s: GO 610 (1985), issued to repatriate non-local employees in Andhra Pradesh, was issued by the government of:
q.x: NTR's government issued GO 610 on 30 December 1985.

q.s: The one-man commission set up in 2001 to examine violations of GO 610 was headed by:
q.x: The Girglani Commission (2001) reported large violations, especially in Zone VI.

q.s: Attirampakkam in Tamil Nadu is an important site of the:
q.x: Attirampakkam, like Hunsgi and Isampur, is a Lower Palaeolithic site.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Lower Palaeolithic site?
q.x: Bagor in Rajasthan is a Mesolithic site.

q.s: In Andhra, the Lower Palaeolithic handaxes, cleavers and choppers were mostly made of:
q.x: Lower Palaeolithic tools were of quartzite; Middle Palaeolithic flakes used chert, jasper and chalcedony.

q.s: Microliths are the characteristic tools of which stage of prehistory?
q.x: Mesolithic tools were microliths of chert and jasper.

q.s: The Nasik Prasasti, which describes the achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni, was issued by his mother:
q.x: Gautami Balasri issued it in Pulumavi's 19th regnal year; Naganika issued the Naneghat inscription.

q.s: The Nasik Prasasti of Gautami Balasri is composed in:
q.x: It is in Prakrit in the Brahmi script.

q.s: Under the Satavahanas, the 'Rajjugahaka' was the:
q.x: The Rajjugahaka (rope-holder) was the surveyor; the Heranika was the treasurer.

q.s: Which of the following Satavahana officers is NOT correctly matched with the duty?
q.x: The Pradeshika was a police officer; the Heranika was the treasurer.

q.s: Which was the strongest guild under the Satavahanas, formed by weavers?
q.x: Kolikas were weavers; Gandhikas perfumers and Tilapishakas oil pressers.

q.s: Which of the following Satavahana guilds is NOT correctly matched with its members?
q.x: Udayantrikas were makers of water machines.

q.s: In early Andhra, the 'Ghatikasthanas' were:
q.x: Ghatikasthanas were Vedic colleges; viharas were Buddhist centres and agraharas were land grants to Brahmins.

q.s: The Gathasaptasati was compiled by the Satavahana king:
q.x: Hala compiled the Gathasaptasati, a collection of about 700 gathas.

q.s: The Gathasaptasati is written in which language?
q.x: It is in Maharashtri Prakrit, though Telugu words such as atta and pilla occur in it.

q.s: The Undavalli, Bhairavakonda and Mogalrajapuram cave temples are credited to the Vishnukundin king:
q.x: These caves are credited to Madhava Varma I; the Vishnukundins built the first Hindu cave temples in the Telugu lands.

q.s: Which of the following statements about cave temples is correct?
o: The Vishnukundins built the first Hindu cave temples in the Telugu lands.
The Udayagiri caves of Madhya Pradesh are Pallava works.
The Undavalli caves were built by the Eastern Chalukya Vishnuvardhana.
q.x: Madhava Varma I is credited with Undavalli; Udayagiri (MP) is Gupta.

q.s: Who ruled the Badami Chalukya kingdom as regent after Kirtivarman I and was later killed by Pulakesin II?
q.x: Mangalesha, Kirtivarman's brother, ruled as regent and was killed by Pulakesin II at Elapattu-Simbige.

q.s: Vatapi, the capital of the early Chalukyas, is modern Badami in which district of Karnataka?
q.x: Badami is in Bagalkot district.

q.s: According to the Badami cliff inscription of 543 CE, Vatapi was fortified by:
q.x: Pulakesin I fortified Vatapi in 543 CE.

q.s: Which Kakatiya ruler took the title 'Andhra Deshadhiswara'?
q.x: Ganapatideva, who united the Telugu lands, was Andhra Deshadhiswara.

q.s: Rudramadevi took the title 'Rayagajakesari' after defeating the:
q.x: She took the title for beating the Yadavas of Devagiri.

q.s: The Ramappa (Rudreswara) temple at Palampet was built in 1213 by:
q.x: Recherla Rudra, general of Ganapatideva, built it; it became a World Heritage Site in 2021.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true of the Ramappa temple?
o: It stands on a star-shaped platform.
It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.
It is known for its floating bricks.
q.x: It was built by Recherla Rudra in 1213 during Ganapatideva's reign.

q.s: Anavema Reddi took Rajahmundry, Pithapuram and Simhachalam after defeating the:
q.x: With the help of the Padmanayakas and Vijayanagara, Anavema beat the Kalinga Gajapatis.

q.s: 'Puriti Pannu', a tax on childbirth, was levied by:
q.x: Racha Vema, the last Kondavidu king, levied it and was killed by his own people.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire?
q.x: Vijayanagara's dynasties were Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu; the Kakatiyas ruled earlier from Warangal.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a capital of the Aravidu dynasty?
q.x: Anegondi was the early Sangama capital; Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore were Aravidu capitals.

q.s: Which Ashtadiggaja poet of Krishnadevaraya's court wrote 'Kalapurnodayamu'?
q.x: Pingali Surana wrote Kalapurnodayamu and the dvyarthi kavya Raghava Pandaviyamu.

q.s: 'Panduranga Mahatmyamu' was written by:
q.x: Tenali Ramakrishna wrote Panduranga Mahatmyamu; Dhurjati wrote Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam.

q.s: In 1639 the English obtained the grant of Madras from:
q.x: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka of Srikalahasti granted Madras to Francis Day of the Machilipatnam council.

q.s: The Englishman who obtained the grant of Madras in 1639 was:
